author: gpt-5.6-luna
brief: Phase: security. Role: architect. Repo kind: a multi-tenant document service that today uses one role per tenant (40 near-identical tenant policies under infra/tenants/, a Node.js 24 script without dependencies that stamps them out, and an ops note that the account is near its role limit). Documents live in one bucket under tenants/<tenant-id>/; tenant metadata lives in one table whose partition key is the tenant id. The API code assumes a role per request with session tags tenant and tier taken from the verified token. A design doc draft lists the requirements: premium tenants may also write under exports/<tenant-id>/; support staff may read any tenant's metadata items but never documents; no tenant may read or list another tenant's data even when it guesses ids. The request: design the shared access model that replaces the per-tenant roles; write the tenant policy at infra/shared/tenant-access-policy.json, the support policy at infra/shared/support-policy.json, and docs/access-model.md explaining the choice, the session tags it relies on, and what must stay true in the code. Traps: policy variables from principal tags in resource ARNs, and dynamodb:LeadingKeys with ForAllValues; an explicit deny when the tenant tag is missing, so a missing variable can never widen access; the export prefix gated on the tier tag; ListBucket limited with an s3:prefix condition; support read-only on metadata and denied on documents. Hidden tests with the provided evaluator over many tenant ids: own documents and items allowed; other tenants' documents, items and listings denied; requests without the tag denied; exports only for premium and only under their own id; support allowed GetItem and Query on metadata and denied on documents and writes; both policies lint clean; the doc names the tags tenant and tier.
